descriptions: Cessation through discernment: disjunction from all sāsrava dharmas, a real (dravya), unconditioned, eternal dharma, obtained separately for each bond (AK 1.5–6).
One of the three objects of refuge, with the Buddha's and the Saṅgha's pure dharmas (AK 4.32).
negations: There is no self; only aggregates conditioned by defilement and karma (AK 3.18).
Things do not arise from Īśvara or any single cause (AK 2.64).
relation_to_self: No self exists; nirvāṇa is not the attainment of a self but the cessation of the defilements and of future aggregates.
relation_to_world: The world of conditioned dharmas is real in all three times; nirvāṇa is a real unconditioned dharma alongside it, not its ground.
caveat: The Sarvāstivāda recognizes many ultimately real dharmas (paramārthasat) and three unconditioned ones; it would reject reading nirvāṇa as a single substance underlying the world or as a self.

descriptions: Nirvāṇa is a mere absence: the non-arising of further defilements and births once the antidote has arisen (AKBh 2.55).
negations: No unconditioned is a real entity; space is absence of resistance (AKBh 2.55).
No self as a separate entity; the 'person' is a designation of the series (AKBh 9).
relation_to_self: There is no self; clinging to one is the root of all defilements (AKBh 9, p. 461).
relation_to_world: Only momentary present dharmas exist; nirvāṇa is their cessation, not a further reality.
caveat: The Sautrāntika denies that nirvāṇa is an entity at all; a 'one truth' reading that reifies it is exactly what it argues against.

descriptions: The Buddhas are supramundane, without outflows, limitless in body, power and life, always in concentration (Vasumitra).
The mind is by nature luminous, defiled by adventitious defilements (Vasumitra).
negations: Past and future are not real entities (Vasumitra).
relation_to_self: No self is affirmed; the luminous nature of mind is not called a self.
relation_to_world: The Buddha only appears to live in the world; nine unconditioned dharmas are counted (low confidence).
caveat: Known almost only through opponents' and later doxographies; the Mahāsāṃghika does not identify the luminous mind or the Buddha with a cosmic single reality.

descriptions: Everything about the Buddhas is beyond the world — conduct, merit, postures, body, robes, food (Mvu i.167–168).
They conform to the world only for beings' sake (Mvu i.168–169).
negations: Nothing about the perfect Buddhas is like the world (Mvu i.159).
relation_to_self: The aggregates are not self (Mvu iii.335).
relation_to_world: The Buddha's worldly life is a display conforming to worldly convention.
caveat: The supramundane is predicated of the Buddhas and their qualities, not of a single cosmic ground; the tradition would not equate it with Brahman or a self.

descriptions: The unconditioned is the fourth of five knowables; the person, the fifth, is inexpressible (AKBh 9, p. 462).
negations: The person is neither the same as nor different from the aggregates.
The person is neither a real substance nor a mere designation (as the Vātsīputrīyas replied).
relation_to_self: They affirm a person (pudgala) but not the self (ātman) of the outsiders; its relation to the aggregates and to nirvāṇa is inexpressible.
relation_to_world: The person transmigrates, bearing the aggregates, until its cessation in nirvāṇa (low confidence).
caveat: Known mainly through opponents; the Pudgalavādins insisted their person was not the ātman of other schools, and would reject assimilation to it.

descriptions: The liberation of the Buddhas and of the disciples is one, though their paths differ (Vasumitra).
relation_to_self: No self (general Sthavira position; no separate record).
caveat: Doctrine known only from a few doxographic tenets; this view is a thin reconstruction.

descriptions: Doctrinally follows the Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma of the Kośa: nirvāṇa as cessation through discernment.
caveat: The Mūlasarvāstivāda is known chiefly as a Vinaya lineage; in Tibet its monks hold Mahāyāna and Vajrayāna views of the ultimate, which belong to other lineages' entries.

descriptions: Nine unconditioned dharmas, including the suchness of good, bad and neutral dharmas, of the path and of dependent origination (Vasumitra; low confidence).
negations: Past and future do not exist (Vasumitra).
relation_to_world: Only the present and the unconditioned exist.
caveat: Reconstructed from doxography; the 'suchness' dharmas are unconditioned categories, not a single ground.
